target_customer: Owners and managers of large commercial real estate portfolios who spend on HVAC maintenance and replacement
problem: Property owners lacked a single record of their HVAC units and had to run bids, repairs and capital replacement by hand, overpaying for projects.
business_model: B2B SaaS priced by building square footage plus procurement of HVAC projects
product_category: Commercial real estate HVAC asset management and procurement software

founders.name: Alex Rangel
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch says the idea came while he worked in Florida as a sales engineer for Trane. Education not found.

founders.name: Chris Ginter
founders.background_notes: Friend of Rangel since high school per TechCrunch. No other background found.

technical_complexity.rationale: The 2014 product tagged equipment with digital barcodes and ran bidding and dispatch workflows. YC page cites 12,800 lines of code at application. Mostly standard web and mobile work with field data capture.

defensibility.rationale: An equipment inventory and vendor relationships create some lock-in once units are tagged, but the software itself was copyable and Ravti had agreements with only one national portfolio manager in 2014.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent copied it early. Building Engines bought Ravti in January 2021 and launched an expanded HVAC module in February 2022 that it said was based on Ravti features.

market_need_then: TechCrunch in August 2014 reported tagged equipment covering 30 million square feet, pricing by square footage, and claimed savings of 18 to 40 percent on HVAC replacement by bulk buying. Demand signal came from founder experience in HVAC sales.

branding.domain_note: Used ravti.com, an exact .com, from the YC listing.

identity.voice_and_tone: Pitch language stressed removing headaches for owners and vendors

brand_strength.rationale: No press or community about the brand itself was found. The name was coined and gave no hint of HVAC; ravti.com returned a 503 at fetch time.

outcome_analysis: Ravti was started by a former HVAC sales engineer and grew to a team of 17 selling to commercial property owners. It was acquired by Building Engines in January 2021, which then became part of JLL in 2021, and Ravti features became the base of Building Engines' HVAC module. Price and funding were not disclosed, so the size of the outcome is unknown.
notes: Seedtable pages show seed rounds dated 2014-08 and 2014-10 with TSVC and Y Combinator named, but no amounts and only an aggregator source, so they are unverified and not recorded as rounds. No competitor named in dated 2014 coverage; TechCrunch only uses KAYAK as an analogy. BusinessWire release returned 403 so the acquisition date comes from search results and the Homebrew post. Website fetch failed with 503.
